Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash-type loss
of motion. The reported mechanism of injury is in keeping with the force and direction of the impact described. Over the course
of care, the patient completed 21 visits that included manual therapy, guided range-of-motion exercises, and a home stretching
program. Symptoms improved steadily, and visit frequency was reduced in step with recovery, following a typical course for this
type of injury. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly support the diagnosis of a cervical soft tissue injury. The
patient also reported a small strain in the same region several years earlier, which resolved completely and had no lasting effect
on function before the collision. Billing records reflect the services rendered without repeated or duplicate charges. At discharge,
the patient had regained most of the expected range of motion, reported minimal residual discomfort, and was advised to continue
independent exercises as needed.
